10-a.question: What variables in the raw data is output Running speed derived from?
10-a.decision_correctness_justification: The AI computes running speed from within-corridor position (ft_PosCum mod corridor_len) using finite differences, rather than using the precomputed ft_RunSpeed field available in the data. The computed speed has very low correlation (r=0.08) with ft_RunSpeed because: (1) within-corridor position wraps at corridor boundaries creating artifacts, (2) gray space movement is not captured in corridor position, and (3) the position resolution at ~3 Hz sampling is very coarse. The ft_RunSpeed field (or ft_RunCum for cumulative distance) captures actual running speed from higher-resolution VR tracking data.
10-a.code_correctness_justification: The code correctly implements its chosen approach (np.diff on position / dt_frame), though the approach itself produces incorrect speed values relative to the actual running speed.

The position derivative approach is flawed because it uses within-corridor position which wraps at corridor boundaries, producing incorrect speed values. The quartile binning approach is correct per the instructions ('4 bins, each corresponding to 25% of the data'), but the underlying speed values are wrong.
10-b.code_correctness_justification: The code correctly implements quartile-based binning on its computed speed values. The np.quantile and np.digitize calls are correct for creating 4 equal-frequency bins.
